evidence: 2026-05: Senator Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli swept APC's direct primary across all 33 Oyo LGAs to become its governorship candidate, beating out minister Adebayo Adelabu's camp (Arise TV); on 2026-07-03 he received his INEC nomination form and unveiled Adesoji Adedeji as running mate (ThisDay).
Incumbent Seyi Makinde (PDP) is term-limited in 2027; one May 2026 report listed Makinde as Accord's presidential candidate (unconfirmed/conflicting), signaling possible PDP-platform turmoil in Oyo.
PDP's national collapse (presidential bench defected to ADC/NDC) weakens the platform defending Oyo; APC holds federal power and most of the southwest, Tinubu's home region.
No Oyo general-election polling found; evidence on the matchup is thin.
0xb582528a5fe14a93da51bba48e709e59ca2773.strongest_opposing_case: Makinde is one of Nigeria's most popular governors and his machine (whatever platform it lands on) can elect a successor; Oyo rejected APC in 2019 and 2023, Alli is a first-time statewide standard-bearer, and southwest APC infighting (Adelabu camp) could depress its vote.
0xb582528a5fe14a93da51bba48e709e59ca2773.reasoning_summary: Base ~40% for the ruling-party nominee against a popular term-limited opposition governor's succession plan. APC's unified ticket, federal/southwest alignment and PDP platform chaos push up; Makinde's personal popularity pushes down. Final 0.38.

base_rate.reference_class: Three-time candidate / far-right standard-bearer winning the French presidency = P(eligible and runs) x P(wins two-round election); Le Pen lost runoffs in 2017 (34%) and 2022 (41.5%)
base_rate.source: French two-round presidential history; RN runoff ceiling

evidence: 2026-07-07: Paris Court of Appeal upheld Le Pen's embezzlement conviction but reduced her ineligibility to 45 months; with 30 months deemed served, ~15 months remained — coverage says a 2027 run 'remains possible' yet the arithmetic (15 months from July 2026 reaches ~Oct 2027, past the April 2027 vote) leaves her eligibility genuinely unclear (Sigmalive/AP).
2026-07: Both Le Pen and the prosecutor general could appeal to the Court of Cassation within 10 days, so the legal outcome was still not final.
Le Pen has said she might not run if constraints make campaigning impractical; RN's designated fallback is Jordan Bardella, who polls at or above her first-round numbers.
2025-2026 polling consistently put the RN candidate (her or Bardella) first in round one (~33-37%), but runoff projections against a unified-center candidate remained close to or below 50%.
0x8126317d621047fb13d508a2651eecc8d38305.strongest_opposing_case: If Cassation suspends or shortens the ban she runs as the round-one favorite amid historic unpopularity of the governing center, repeated RN runoff gains (34->41.5%) suggest the ceiling is gone, and a fragmented left could hand her a winnable runoff opponent.
0x8126317d621047fb13d508a2651eecc8d38305.reasoning_summary: Decompose: P(eligible and is the RN candidate) ~0.40 given the ambiguous 15-remaining-months ruling and Bardella alternative; P(wins | runs) ~0.35 on strong round-one but unresolved runoff math. 0.40 x 0.35 ~ 0.14; round to 0.13.

base_rate.reference_class: Third-party/minor-platform candidate defeating an incumbent president in Nigeria; no Nigerian president has lost to a candidate outside the two dominant structures
base_rate.source: Nigerian presidential elections 1999-2023 (only incumbent loss: Jonathan to APC's unified mega-coalition, 2015)

evidence: 2025-12-31: Peter Obi left the Labour Party and later joined the small Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC); 2026-05-29: NDC ratified him as its presidential candidate (Daily Trust/kolaking).

2026-05: The opposition 'coalition' fractured — Atiku won the ADC primary (1.85M votes) while Obi went NDC and Labour picked Chibuzo Okereke; allAfrica (2026-05-26) describes opposition parties 'in disarray' with factional candidates.
Obi took 25% and ~6.1M votes in 2023 on the Labour platform; the NDC has far less national structure, polling agents, or state-level machinery.
Election set for Jan 16, 2027; a runoff is possible if no candidate meets the 25%-in-24-states spread, but Obi's vote is regionally concentrated (southeast/south-south plus urban centers).
0xe00cb03a0aefe8f4a06338da171a8df62edd20.strongest_opposing_case: Economic hardship under Tinubu is severe and broad, Obi retains the most enthusiastic personal following in the country, and a first-ever runoff scenario in a fragmented field could let him consolidate the entire anti-Tinubu vote in a head-to-head.
0xe00cb03a0aefe8f4a06338da171a8df62edd20.reasoning_summary: Base ~5% for a minor-platform challenger vs an incumbent. Obi's proven 25% base and anti-incumbent mood argue up; the three-way opposition split (Atiku/ADC, Obi/NDC, LP), his weak party machinery, and the geographic-spread requirement argue down. Final 0.06.

base_rate.reference_class: Incumbent Nigerian president seeking re-election; incumbents won 1999, 2003, 2011, 2019 and lost only 2015 (to a unified opposition mega-merger)
base_rate.source: Nigerian presidential incumbency record 1999-2023

evidence: 2026-05-24: Tinubu won the APC presidential primary with ~11.0M affirmation votes against token opposition (Channels TV).

2026-05-26: Opposition is fractured three-plus ways — Atiku (ADC), Obi (NDC), Okereke (LP), plus minor parties; allAfrica describes 'disarray' and factional candidates, the opposite of the unified 2015 template that beat an incumbent.
2025-26: Wave of PDP governors and senators defected to APC, giving Tinubu control of most state machineries ahead of the Jan 16, 2027 vote.
Tinubu won 2023 with only 36.6% in a three-way race; the 2027 field is even more fragmented, and the 25%-spread rule plus runoff provisions favor the structure-rich incumbent.
0xdb66349b5658e7ce54667294bb61ca2f98d68f.strongest_opposing_case: Severe cost-of-living pain, fuel-subsidy and naira-reform fallout make Tinubu genuinely unpopular; if hardship drives a historic protest wave or the opposition executes a late single-candidate alliance (as in 2015), an incumbent can lose — it has happened once.
0xdb66349b5658e7ce54667294bb61ca2f98d68f.reasoning_summary: Base ~80% for an incumbent. The fragmented opposition (Atiku/Obi split confirmed at May 2026 primaries), mass defections to APC, and incumbent control of electoral machinery push above base; economic anger and low 2023 vote share temper it. Final 0.78.
